title: Prince Harry and Celebrities Face Huge Legal Bill After Losing Privacy Case
summary:
Imagine losing a game and then having to pay a huge penalty. That's kind of what happened to Prince Harry and six other famous people in a court case in England. They sued the publisher of the Daily Mail newspaper, saying the paper did bad things to get private information about them. But the judge didn't agree and threw out their case in July.

Now, the judge has made another decision: Prince Harry and the others have to pay the newspaper's legal costs, which could be as much as £34.5 million! That's about $45 million. The judge said the way they presented their claims was "unreasonable to a high degree." He was upset that they didn't withdraw some serious accusations even when they didn't have enough proof.

The other people in the case are Sir Elton John and his husband David Furnish, former politician Sir Simon Hughes, campaigner Baroness Lawrence, and actresses Sadie Frost and Liz Hurley. They had insurance to cover up to £16.2 million of the costs, but now they might have to pay around £18 million out of their own pockets.

The judge, Mr. Justice Nicklin, said the £34 million claim seemed "excessive" but he decided not to set a limit on what the newspaper can recover. He said it was "striking" that not one serious allegation was voluntarily withdrawn by the group. He said serious accusations of criminality can't just be left hanging over people.

The newspaper's publisher called the ruling "a devastating critique of an attempt to destroy a newspaper." Prince Harry and Baroness Lawrence said in a statement, "We came to court seeking justice and accountability. But we have received neither." They have until October 2 to try to appeal. This is a big deal because it shows that even famous people can face huge consequences when they lose a court case.
why_it_matters: This story shows that in real life, making serious accusations without enough proof can have big consequences, just like breaking rules in a game can cost your team.

background_read: In many countries, when someone loses a civil lawsuit, a judge can order them to pay the other side's legal fees.
Prince Harry is a member of the British royal family, and Sir Elton John is a famous British singer; both are public figures who often appear in newspapers.
The Daily Mail is a well-known British newspaper, and U.K. privacy law lets people take newspapers to court if they think private information was obtained illegally.
Article_Structure: WHO: Prince Harry, Sir Elton John, David Furnish, Sir Simon Hughes, Baroness Lawrence, Sadie Frost, and Liz Hurley.
WHAT: A judge ordered them to pay the Daily Mail publisher's legal costs, possibly £34.5 million, after their privacy case was thrown out.
WHERE: In a court in England, after the earlier July ruling.
WHY: The judge said their claims were presented unreasonably and serious accusations were not withdrawn even without enough proof.
